searchText: Would you need to reseal or would you just need to try-append txs without the state root from the resulting payload ever being necessary to compute? To clarify, this is for newPayload coming with IL txs, right? yes, to phrase it differently, how much time / work does the EL need to do to apply additional txs on top of an already prepared payload Gotcha, we're talking about building here, not attesting. we "seal" in a few ms, or also sub-ms, depending on hw. But we are anyway redesigning the whole build, so I would not focus too much on those values. The flow would be like: EL starts building -> CL submits more IL relevant txs to the EL -> EL has to include them -> EL computes state root -> CL submits more IL txs -> EL has to include and redo state root. Is that describing the "challenge" that ELs might face, <@586161934425128960> ? Or simpler, ELs required to be flexible in their building process if CLs deliver new IL txs exactly, and based on how easy that is for EL we can adjust our fcu behavior, I am mostly wondering what we should do if we see IL really late, likely we can just ignore them, but as a proposer you wanna satisfy as many IL as possible
